@dummdidumm sorry about the confusion. The `https` comes from [HTTPie](https://httpie.io/). I've double-checked and confirmed the issue. Here is the screenshot of headers when the app running in dev mode (`pnpm run dev`). The headers are present: And here is a screenshot of the app that runs in production mode (`pnpm run preview`). The headers are absent: Please let me know if you get different results. ohhh.... this must be because of https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/pull/8131.

Two options:

1. we treat this as a bug and revert #8131 
2. add `export const prerender = false` alongside `export const ssr = false`

#8131 is a valuable optimisation so it would be a shame to lose it, but I wonder how we can make this behaviour clearer.
Is there the possibility of a third option where we somehow check if `setHeaders` is invoked and opt out of prerendering in that case, too, or would that contain too many false positives?

No, that seems like a pretty good solution as long as it's documented (you could always opt back in with `prerender = true`). There's still the possibility that someone could do `response.headers.set(...)` after calling `resolve` in `handle` — don't know if we'd want to deoptimize in that case as well

issue.title: `prerender` setting in empty `server.js` causes request errors despite the page working in browser
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

When
```js
export const prerender = true;

// No other content in file
```
is used in a `server.ts` file that does not contain any other code, the site appears to be working fine in browsers (no errors on page or in network tab).

However, external tools (e.g. Google Search Console, sitemap generators  or simply `curl`) will report a `40x: Method not allowed` error.

This can be fixed by adding an empty `GET()`  method in the same file, like so:

```js
export const prerender = 'auto';

export async function GET() {
	return new Response();
}
```

The [docs](https://kit.svelte.dev/docs/page-options#prerender) don't mention that this is necessary, and it's very confusing that some tools claim the site doesn't work. 

This bug may be a variant or generalization of #8428 



### Reproduction

1. Create a route with a dummy `+page.svelte`, an empty `+server.js` and add `export const prerender = true;`
2. Run `build` and then `preview`
3. Call `curl http://<your-route>`

Expected: No errors.
Actual:  Curl responds with `GET method not allowed` 



### Logs

```Shell
Based on the example above:

curl http://localhost:4173
GET method not allowed

Google Search Console reports:

"Failed: Blocked due to other 4xx issue"
```

issue.title: '$env/dynamic/public' variables don't get loaded if ssr = false.
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

If you use `'$env/dynamic/public'` to import variables from `process.env` when `export const ssr = false;`, but prerendering is not explicitly disabled, the variables won't be sent to the client.

This is (I assume) because the html file is prerendered at build time, and uses the build-time variables. At runtime, it doesn't update the html file with the new values of process.env.

This works if `export const prerender = false` is set.

issue.title: Prerendered +server routes don't use the specified HTTP response headers
issue.body:
### Describe the bug

Prerendering a `+server.ts` file causes its HTTP response headers to be ignored.

E.g., I want to prerender an atom.xml file for a blog site. I'd like to override the `Cache-Control` and `Content-Type` headers. When I add `export const prerender = true` and run `pnpm preview`, this page renders with `content-type: text/html` and no `cache-control` header at all:

```ts
import type { RequestHandler } from './$types';

export const prerender = true;

export const GET: RequestHandler = async ({ url }) => {
  const body =
    '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>\n<feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">\n</feed>';
  const headers = {
    'Cache-Control': `max-age=0, must-revalidate`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/atom+xml',
  };
  return new Response(body, {
    status: 200,
    headers,
  });
};
```

Workaround is to only prerender HTML pages since their content type is `text/html`, and only those that don't need header overrides such as `Cache-Control`.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/BMorearty/sveltekit-prerender-headers

Clone this repo and build it for production (bug does not reproduce in dev mode):
`$ pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm preview`

Then in your browser, open the Network debug panel.

Then go to http://localhost:4173/atom.xml. Note in the Network panel that the `Content-Type`
is `text/html` when i should be `application/atom+xml`, and there is no `Cache-Control`
header. Both headers are specified in `/src/routes/atom.xml/+server.ts` but are being ignored.

Also note that atom.xml renders as an HTML page, not as XML. That's due to the incorrect
`Content-Type`.
